address.description:
The static external IP address represented by this resource.
The IP address must be inside the specified subnetwork,
if any. Set by the API if undefined.
address.rationale: This argument specifies the static IP address to reserve. IP addressing is specific to each team's network design, and constraining it to a particular value would be overreaching rather than a generic security control.

address_type.description:
The type of address to reserve.
Note: if you set this argument's value as 'INTERNAL' you need to leave the 'network_tier' argument unset in that resource block. Default value: "EXTERNAL" Possible values: ["INTERNAL", "EXTERNAL"]
address_type.rationale: This argument determines whether the reserved IP address is internal or external. Requiring INTERNAL addresses where public connectivity is unnecessary reduces unintended network exposure and provides a valid platform-level security policy.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether the reserved address can be deleted, protected from deletion, or abandoned from Terraform management. Accidental deletion can disrupt dependent network services, while abandonment can create an unmanaged resource; a platform-level policy can therefore require approved deletion behaviour.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: This argument provides human-readable metadata about the address and does not affect access, network exposure, encryption, or the security of the resource.

ip_collection.description:
Reference to the source of external IPv4 addresses, like a PublicDelegatedPrefix(PDP) for BYOIP.
The PDP must support enhanced IPv4 allocations.
Use one of the following formats to specify a PDP when reserving an external IPv4 address using BYOIP.
Full resource URL, as in:
  * 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{{projectId}}/regions/{{region}}/publicDelegatedPrefixes/{{pdp-name}}'
Partial URL, as in:
  * 'projects/{{projectId}}/regions/region/publicDelegatedPrefixes/{{pdp-name}}'
  * 'regions/{{region}}/publicDelegatedPrefixes/{{pdp-name}}'
ip_collection.rationale: This argument references the IP collection from which the address is allocated. The appropriate collection is specific to each team's network design, and platform policy should not constrain references to particular delegated prefixes or internal ranges.

ip_version.description: The IP Version that will be used by this address. The default value is 'IPV4'. Possible values: ["IPV4", "IPV6"]
ip_version.rationale: This argument specifies whether the reserved address uses IPv4 or IPv6. The appropriate IP version depends on the organisation's network architecture and compatibility requirements rather than a universal security policy.

ipv6_endpoint_type.description:
The endpoint type of this address, which should be VM or NETLB. This is
used for deciding which type of endpoint this address can be used after
the external IPv6 address reservation. Possible values: ["VM", "NETLB"]
ipv6_endpoint_type.rationale: This argument defines the IPv6 endpoint type for the reserved address. The correct value depends on workload-specific networking requirements and does not represent a universal platform security control.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this address.  A list of key->value pairs.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: This argument assigns metadata labels to the address resource for organisation and management purposes. Labels improve administration but do not directly influence authentication, authorisation, network exposure or data protection.

name.description:
Name of the resource. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and
comply with RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters
long and match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?'
which means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all
following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit,
except the last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: This argument specifies the resource name used to identify the address. Naming conventions are organisation-specific and do not directly affect authentication, authorisation, network exposure or data security.

network.description:
The URL of the network in which to reserve the address. This field
can only be used with INTERNAL type with the VPC_PEERING and
IPSEC_INTERCONNECT purposes.
network.rationale: This argument specifies the VPC network associated with the reserved address. The appropriate network is specific to each organisation's infrastructure and should not be constrained by a universal platform security policy.

network_tier.description:
The networking tier used for configuring this address. If this field is not
specified, it is assumed to be PREMIUM.
This argument should not be used when configuring Internal addresses, because [network tier cannot be set for internal traffic; it's always Premium](https://cloud.google.com/network-tiers/docs/overview). Possible values: ["PREMIUM", "STANDARD"]
network_tier.rationale: This argument specifies the network tier used by the reserved address. The appropriate tier depends on performance, routing and cost requirements rather than a universal platform security policy.

prefix_length.description: The prefix length if the resource represents an IP range.
prefix_length.rationale: This argument specifies the size of the reserved IP address range. The appropriate prefix length depends on organisational network planning and does not represent a universal security control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This argument specifies the Google Cloud project where the address resource is created. Project selection depends on the organisation's environment and is not a universal platform security control.

purpose.description:
The purpose of this resource, which can be one of the following values.

* GCE_ENDPOINT for addresses that are used by VM instances, alias IP
ranges, load balancers, and similar resources.

* SHARED_LOADBALANCER_VIP for an address that can be used by multiple
internal load balancers.

* VPC_PEERING for addresses that are reserved for VPC peer networks.

* IPSEC_INTERCONNECT for addresses created from a private IP range that
are reserved for a VLAN attachment in an HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect
configuration. These addresses are regional resources.

* PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT for a private network address that is used to
configure Private Service Connect. Only global internal addresses can use
this purpose.

This should only be set when using an Internal address.
purpose.rationale: This argument specifies the intended networking purpose of the reserved address. The appropriate value depends on the workload and networking architecture rather than a universal platform security policy.

region.description:
The Region in which the created address should reside.
If it is not provided, the provider region is used.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

subnetwork.description:
The URL of the subnetwork in which to reserve the address. If an IP
address is specified, it must be within the subnetwork's IP range.
This field can only be used with INTERNAL type with
GCE_ENDPOINT/DNS_RESOLVER purposes.
subnetwork.rationale: This argument specifies the subnetwork associated with the reserved address. The appropriate subnetwork depends on the organisation's network architecture and should not be constrained by a universal platform security policy.
